title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political impersonation carried out with a generative video tool. The videos were posted to a public social media account and showed a candidate saying things she never said, which places the failure at the point of publication rather than at the point of generation. The generator applied an automatic label identifying the content as AI-made, so the platform disclosed the synthetic origin while the false statements themselves went out as if they were real speech.

Catching this would not have required a technical fix. The material was labelled as AI-generated at the moment it was posted, so the deception was visible to anyone who read the label. What was absent was any step between generation and publication in which a person declined to publish fabricated statements attributed to a named opponent. The label addresses the question of how the video was made, not the question of whether its content is true.

The cease-and-desist letter is an allegation by Cooke's attorneys, not a finding by a court, and no defamation claim has been adjudicated. Whether the videos were intended to deceive voters is asserted in the letter and denied by Van Orden's campaign, and intent is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip from Aug. 4 that the letter calls pure fiction. The videos carry an automatic label noting they were made with an AI generator called Grok Imagine.

Cooke's attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that the false content aims to fool voters and harm Cooke's reputation, and warned that Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law. The letter says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring Van Orden's accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded on social media with another AI video featuring a duck saying cease and desist.
